about: STACK-V8 (v7 + clear exit). 27.4-36.33 s replaced by a CEM-optimised exit (make_stack_v8_exit.py): speed <= 6.5 m/s, stack out of frame by ~31 s, framing converges on the animatic attention view (cluster + feed, sand) by 30.5 s; rejoins the animatic at 36.33 s (at rest). v7 kept as camera-path-stack_v7.json. STACK-V6 (EXPLODED STACK, eye-level hold) VARIANT. LAYERS stack-v6 camera variant (v6: the closed hold goes back to the ref eye-level 3/4: level camera at ~40% of the stack height with lens shift; copy area cleaned by the scene_rules in stack-explode.json, not by the vantage; explode keys + exit as v5). v5 doc: -> camera-path-stack.json (camera-path.json untouched; v4 kept as camera-path-stack_v4.json). Identical to the animatic path for t <= T_IN and t >= T_OUT (C1 Hermite joins on the animatic's own velocities). 16.5-19.6: rise out of the input beat to an ELEVATED level camera (straight verticals, lens shift) SSW of the stack: from there the input dicer/conveyor, the attention feed and spheres are behind the stack or out of frame, so the right 45% is clean sand (ray-cast verified). 19.6-20.4: closed stack at the ref framing (cap ~8% from the top, plate ~88%, stack centre at 0.335 W). 20.4-28.6: WIDE exploded-diagram camera: target = centre of the window [box below .. block above] of the opening layer, gentle look-down, slow steady dolly up, orbit 22 -> 46 deg stack-local (24 deg total), lens fitted so the window fills ~88% of the height. 28.6-T_OUT: exit past the cap's east side and descend into the attention scene, >= 10 m from every stack part, speed capped ~6 m/s; rejoin when it fits the speed cap. Original: animatic/camera-path.json. PrimeArc animatic camera path. One continuous camera, site scroll order. Blender world units = metres, Z up; *_threejs fields are converted to three.js Y-up (x, z, -y). FOV: sensor 36 mm wide; vfov for a 16:10 frame. Interpolation between keys: per-channel cubic Bezier with auto-clamped handles (ease in/out, a repeated key = hold); orientation = lookAt(target) with world up. 'shift' = lens shift (fraction of frame width) used to offset the hero subject right of centre (three.js: camera.setViewOffset). 'samples' = the exact evaluated camera for every frame at 24 fps.
